positions.as_written: Take the history: the age, whether the knee snaps audibly, whether it has ever locked, and whether the child can straighten it fully.
Ask the parent as well as the child, since a snapping knee is often noticed by an observer first.
Measure the extension carefully, comparing with the other side, since a small deficit is the common finding.
Take the knee through the range with a hand on the lateral joint line, feeling for a palpable clunk.
